policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the plural 'his servants,' distinguishing the qere plural from the ketiv singular 'his servant.'

ASV has the plural construction 'cities which are not inhabited,' distinguishing the qere plural נוֹשָׁבוּ from the ketiv feminine singular נושבה; the alternative-rendering note concerns 'unto' and does not decide this unit.
ASV addresses a second-person feminine inhabitant ('O inhabitant ... thou'), reinforced by the Hebrew-gloss note 'inhabitress,' distinguishing qere יֹשַׁבְתְּ from ketiv first-person ישבתי.
ASV's second-person wording 'that makest thy nest' distinguishes qere מְקֻנַּנְתְּ from ketiv first-person מקננתי.
